full_judgment: 42. Question of practising fraud in executing and registering a sale deed in respect of a plot of land is a serious question of fact which can only be thrashed out on evidence to be produced by the contending parties in a properly constituted suit and it is definitely the domain of the civil Court to decide such fact but not RAJUK or its officials. In the context, it will not be out of place to state the law that the onus to prove fraud is squarely upon the party who alleges it and a registered document has a presumption of correctness under clause (e) of section 114 of the Evidence Act and it needs judicial decision. And RAJUK has not been vested with such judicial power. Neither Mr Mahbubey Alam nor Mr Tobarak Hossain, could show any provision of law which authorized RAJUK or writ-respondent No. 1 to venture upon to decide the dispute as to the true ownership of a plot of land between the lessees (writ-respondent Nos. 4 and 5) and the transferee (the writ-petitioner) as sought by the impugned letter. Only because the writ-petitioner appeared before writ-respondent No. 1 pursuant to the impugned letter, he could not be debarred from challenging the propriety or legality of the same before the High Court Division by filing the writ petition in question when the impugned letter was issued without having any legal backing. In the context, the High Court Division rightly declared the same to have been issued without lawful authority and was of no legal effect and, as such, no interference is called for with the judgment and order passed by it in Writ Petition No. 58 of 2008, we find no merit in CP No. 864 of 2010.
